LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.statisticTripleLa: Under source law p, the statistic triple law is the joint distribution of the parameter Θ, the statistic T(X), and the original observation X, in that order.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.IsSufficientStati: For a given source law, T is sufficient for Θ based on X when Θ and X are conditionally independent given T(X).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isSufficientStati: Under the fixed source law, T is sufficient for Θ based on X if and only if the reverse chain Θ → T(X) → X is Markov.
For finite parameter, observation and statistic alphabets under a fixed law, T is sufficient for Θ exactly when I(Θ;X | T(X)) = 0.
For finite-valued Θ, X and T(X) under the given law, T is sufficient for Θ based on X exactly when I(Θ;T(X)) = I(Θ;X).
For finite-valued Θ, X and T(X) under the given law, T is sufficient for Θ based on X exactly when H(Θ | X) = H(Θ | T(X)).

For a finite observation alphabet, T is sufficient under the given law exactly when there is a channel R from statistic values to observations such that sampling (Θ,T(X)) from its marginal and then drawing from R at T(X) reproduces the full joint law of (Θ,T(X),X).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.exists_marginal_r: If X has a finite alphabet and T is sufficient under the given law, some channel R from statistic values to observations maps the distribution of T(X) back to the distribution of X.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.IsSufficientChann: A channel W is sufficient for the family of laws Pₜ if one recovery channel R works for every t: draw Y under the output law of Pₜ through W and then draw X from R given Y. The resulting law of (Y,X) must equal the original output–input joint law for Pₜ and W.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.IsSufficientStati: A statistic T is sufficient for a family of probability mass functions Pₜ if there is a single recovery channel R that works for every parameter t. For X with law Pₜ, draw S with the law of T(X), then draw X′ from R given S. The pair (S,X′) must have the same law as (T(X),X).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isSufficientStati: The identity statistic, which returns the original observation, is sufficient for every model family.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isMarkovChainOf_o: Let W be a sufficient channel for a family of probability mass functions Pₜ. Draw the parameter Θ from any prior probability mass function. Given Θ = t, draw X from Pₜ, then draw Y through W given X. Under this joint law, Θ → Y → X is a Markov chain.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condMutualInfo_eq: With finite parameter, observation and output alphabets, a channel W sufficient for Pₜ gives I(Θ;X | Y) = 0 for every prior on Θ, when X is drawn from the model and Y through W.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mutualInfo_eq_of_: For finite alphabets, a sufficient channel preserves the information in the observation about the parameter under every prior: drawing X from PΘ and Y through W gives I(Θ;Y) = I(Θ;X).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.condEntropy_eq_of: For finite alphabets, a sufficient channel preserves the uncertainty about Θ under every prior: drawing X from PΘ and Y through W gives H(Θ | X) = H(Θ | Y).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isSufficientChann: Suppose X has finite alphabet and a fixed prior gives every parameter value positive probability. A channel W on the observation is sufficient for the entire family exactly when Θ → Y → X is Markov under this prior, where X is drawn from PΘ and Y through W.
For a finite nonempty parameter set and finite observation alphabet, W is sufficient for the model family exactly when Θ → Y → X is Markov for every prior, with X drawn from PΘ and Y through W.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.isSufficientStati: If X is finite-valued and a fixed prior assigns positive mass to every parameter value, T is sufficient for the model family exactly when Θ and X are conditionally independent given T(X) under that prior.

For a finite nonempty parameter set and finite observation alphabet, T is sufficient for the family Pₜ if and only if Θ and X are conditionally independent given T(X) under every prior on Θ and the model law X given Θ.

On a finite nonempty observation alphabet, T is sufficient for the family Pₜ exactly when there exist finite nonnegative functions g and h such that Pₜ(x) = g(t,T(x)) h(x) for every parameter t and observation x. The same h works for every t.
